title: A minimum of the area at t = 0 forces a nonnegative second variation (abstract form)
statement: Minimality implies nonnegative second variation. Data: P ∈ ℕ; a measure μ on ℝ^P; E ⊆ ℝ^P; J : ℝ → ℝ^P → ℝ (written J(t,x) := J t x); q : ℝ^P → ℝ; B, C, t₀ ∈ ℝ. Hypotheses: E is measurable and μ(E) < ∞; t₀ > 0; q is a.e.-strongly measurable with respect to μ restricted to E, and |q(x)| ≤ B for every x ∈ E; for every t with |t| < t₀, μ(E) ≤ ∫⁻_E ofReal(J(t,x)) dμ(x) and J(t,x) ≤ 1 + (t²/2)q(x) + C|t|³ for every x ∈ E. Conclusion: ∫_E q dμ ≥ 0.
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (E : Set (Euclid P)) (J : ℝ → Euclid P → ℝ) (q : Euclid P → ℝ) (B C t₀ : ℝ), MeasurableSet E → μ E ≠ ∞ → 0 < t₀ → AEStronglyMeasurable q (μ.restrict E) → (∀ x ∈ E, |q x| ≤ B) → (∀ t : ℝ, |t| < t₀ → μ E ≤ ∫⁻ x in E, ENNReal.ofReal (J t x) ∂μ) → (∀ t : ℝ, |t| < t₀ → ∀ x ∈ E, J t x ≤ 1 + t ^ 2 / 2 * q x + C * |t| ^ 3) → 0 ≤ ∫ x in E, q x ∂μ
